title: Overs 7–11: the overlooked tactical phase that’s changing the T20 game
subtitle: A 2017–21 vs 2022–25 comparison of batter intent, bowling mix, and who wins the matchup in the transitional overs.
description: A 2017–21 vs 2022–25 comparison of batter intent, bowling mix, and who wins the matchup in the transitional overs.
blocks: Powerplay and death overs get the headlines. But the modern game is being decided in the *transition*: overs 7 to 11, where intent, matchups and line-up construction combine to create outsized advantages. Since 2022 we see batters take more risk earlier, and teams respond by using different bowl styles to punish or restrict them.
**Why I worked on the phase to 7–11?**
While most analysts look at Overs 7-15 as a monolith, the data suggests we are looking at two entirely different phases.
From over 12 onwards, the “Death-over” mindset starts creeping in. The 7-11 window is where the game behaves strikingly different.
The Statistical Jump: Risk is the New Reward
Comparing T20I data from 2017-2021 to 2022-2025 the evolution is clear. The Strike Rate in this phase has jumped from **119.58 to 124.35**.
More importantly, B**oundary run share** in the 7-11 phase has soared from **47% to 52.5%** Batters aren’t just looking for gaps anymore; they are looking for the ropes earlier than ever.
The Death of the “Safe” Top Order
One of the most telling trends is *who* is facing the balls.
- **The Trend:** The Top 3 are facing a smaller percentage of balls in this phase, while positions 4 through 7 have seen a significant spike.

- **The Tactical Why:** Teams are building massive batting depth, giving the middle-order a “cushion” to take high-risk options against spin. Spinners have less economy in all 4 phases of a T20 inning. In future too, teams will be increasingly bowling more overs of spin to restrict the run scoring and as a result, the role of specialist 'Spin Hitter' increases like the role Shivam Dube, Rajat Patidar play for their team.
The Bowling Matrix: Spin vs. Pace
While batters have figured out Pace (SR against pace jumped from 126 to 133), **Spinners remain the primary decelerators.**
- **The Leg-Break (LB) Struggle:** With teams stacking Left-Handed Batters (LHBs), standard Leg-Break bowlers without a lethal googly are being targeted.

- **The Mystery Spinner (LBG) Edge:** This is where the “False Shot” data gets interesting. Mystery spinners have seen a **+5.33% increase in False Shots** produced because they can turn the ball away from both RHBs and LHBs.
- **Off-Spin’s Lethality:** Not only are Off-spinners keeping it tight, but their **Bowling Strike Rate has plummeted from 32.9 to 26.4.** They aren’t just containing; they are the new wicket-takers.

- **The Chinaman Asset:** Bowlers like Kuldeep Yadav remain essential. Even as batting aggression increases, Chinaman bowlers have maintained an **Economy of 6.8** and a lethal **Strike Rate of 19.1.** In a world of left-handed dominance, the ball turning away from the LHB is the ultimate gold mine.
Interestingly, despite the increase in SR, the **False Shot % has risen across all batting positions.**

Batters are accepting a higher probability of failure in exchange for a higher scoring rate. For a fielding coach, this is a massive signal: **the 7-11 phase is no longer about ‘containment’, it is a primary wicket-taking opportunity.**

"The 'quiet period' is dead. Between overs 7 and 11, T20 cricket has become a game of high-variance chaos where the only crime is standing still. We used to call this the 'accumulation' phase; now, it’s just the 'destruction' phase with a different name. The safety net is gone. The batting depth is terrifying. Welcome to the new T20 trench.
